limitations: Pattern-based triage only. Findings require manual validation; absence of findings does not prove security.

findings.title: Application is debuggable
findings.description: Debug builds can expose runtime state and facilitate instrumentation.

findings.title: Application backup is enabled
findings.description: Backups may expose app data depending on Android version and backup configuration.
findings.remediation: Review backup rules and set android:allowBackup="false" when backups are not required.

findings.title: Cleartext network traffic is permitted
findings.description: The app permits HTTP traffic, which can expose data to network interception.
findings.remediation: Set android:usesCleartextTraffic="false" and use HTTPS for all endpoints.

findings.title: Sensitive permission requested: android.permission.WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE
findings.description: This permission is sensitive or broad and should be justified by a clear feature need.
findings.remediation: Remove unused permissions and request the minimum permissions required.

findings.title: Sensitive permission requested: android.permission.READ_SMS
findings.description: This permission is sensitive or broad and should be justified by a clear feature need.
findings.remediation: Remove unused permissions and request the minimum permissions required.

findings.title: Exported activity: .AdminPanel
findings.description: An exported component may be reachable by other apps; access controls must be checked.
findings.remediation: Set android:exported="false" if external access is not needed, or protect it with appropriate permissions.

findings.title: Potential hardcoded key or secret
findings.description: A constant resembling a cryptographic key or secret appears in source code.
findings.remediation: Do not embed reusable secrets in client apps; use server-side secret management or Android Keystore for device-held keys.

findings.title: Weak hash algorithm
findings.description: MD5 and SHA-1 are not suitable for modern security-sensitive hashing.
findings.remediation: For passwords, use a salted password KDF such as Argon2id, scrypt, bcrypt, or PBKDF2 with suitable parameters.

findings.title: Weak cipher or ECB mode
findings.description: DES is obsolete and ECB mode can reveal patterns in encrypted data.
findings.remediation: Use authenticated encryption such as AES-GCM with nonce management and platform-managed keys.

findings.title: HTTP endpoint in source
findings.description: An HTTP URL is not encrypted in transit and may expose requests or responses.
findings.remediation: Use HTTPS with valid certificate validation; disable cleartext traffic unless a documented exception is required.

findings.title: Sensitive data in logs
findings.evidence: Log.d(TAG, "Attempting authentication for user: " + username + " with password: " + password);
findings.description: Logging authentication or secret-related data may expose it through device logs.
findings.remediation: Remove sensitive values from logs; avoid logging credentials and tokens in all builds.

findings.title: Hardcoded credential check
findings.description: A known credential string is compared directly in client-side logic.
findings.remediation: Perform authentication and authorization on a trusted backend; never embed fixed user credentials in the app.

findings.title: Use of SharedPreferences
findings.description: SharedPreferences is not automatically insecure, but sensitive values stored without encryption require review.
findings.remediation: Do not store passwords or long-lived tokens in plaintext preferences; use an appropriate secure storage design.

findings.title: Sensitive value written to preferences
findings.evidence: editor.putString("password", password); // Stored in cleartext in shared_prefs/credentials.xml
findings.description: A secret-like value is written to preferences; confirm whether it is encrypted and necessary.
findings.remediation: Avoid storing passwords. For tokens, use short lifetimes and platform-backed secure storage.
